:rotating_light: _new alert — needs human_
Channel: `alert-runtime-monitoring`  -  confidence: 0.55  -  bug-type guess: env

*Symptoms:*
• Complete APM telemetry blackout across `runtime-core-api`, `designer-core-api`, and `ms-gateway-api` for the past 6+ hours — Datadog returns empty series for both hits and error rates
• `[Synthetics] Method UI Grid and Dropdown Performance Test Evening run` in *Alert* state since 2026-05-04 00:04 UTC (performance thresholds exceeded, not a 503/outage error)
• `[Synthetics] Method UI Grid and Dropdown Performance Test Day run` in *No Data* since 00:01 UTC (test runner has no data)
• `Service Signup Availability SLO` in Alert (ongoing from 2026-04-29)
• Six runtime-core-api monitors stuck in *No Data*: error-rate, p90 latency, p95 screen-load, p95 action-execution, throughput anomaly — all last fired around 2026-05-03 00:09–00:46 UTC (yesterday midnight same window)
• ES logs unavailable (403 host-not-allowlisted)
*Trace IDs:* none — APM silent, no traces in window

*Time window queried:* 2026-05-04 00:01–01:06 UTC (6h window for golden signals)

*Comparison vs 24h baseline:* 24h-ago window also returns empty series for runtime-core-api. Pattern may be a recurring overnight APM gap or the service has been down since yesterday midnight.

*Recent deploys:* Last runtime-core commit was `b1f9358` on 2026-05-01 (reverted a currency-symbol feature) — 3 days ago, unlikely to be the cause.

*Likely cause:* Two competing hypotheses:
1. *Datadog agent stopped* on the prod Windows host (~midnight UTC) — services may be running fine but sending no telemetry. Synthetics "Alert" (degraded performance, not hard failure) is mildly consistent with services still up.
2. *runtime-core IIS app pool and/or ms-gateway-api stopped* — consistent with No Data (no traffic = no traces). Synthetics performance failures could be frontend-only tests that degrade without backend.
*Suggested next action:* Check IIS app pool status for `runtime-core` and `ms-gateway-api` on the prod server; verify Datadog agent service is running on prod host (`Get-Service DatadogAgent`). If pools stopped, restart and monitor. If Datadog agent stopped, restart and confirm telemetry resumes.

*Centreon Monitoring alert — 04:39 EDT (08:39 UTC)*
_Note: alert body was in Slack blocks only; text field was empty. Investigation based on Datadog metrics._

*Symptoms:*
• `prod-new-04` sustained CPU spike: ~49% user CPU from 08:23–08:38 UTC (15 min), peaking at 59%
• CPU system peaked at 16.7% during same window (elevated kernel activity)
• *Self-resolved at 08:38 UTC — 1 minute before Centreon posted the alert*
• IIS connections remained stable (27–31) throughout; no IIS pool recycle (uptime = 3.3 days)
• No DD errors from `runtime-core-api` or other services during the spike window
• ES unavailable during investigation (403: host not in allowlist)
*24h baseline comparison:*
• Yesterday 08:22–08:38 UTC on `prod-new-04`: max CPU 53%, avg 44% — *identical daily pattern*
• This is very likely a daily scheduled job or maintenance task (SQL Server agent job, Windows Task Scheduler, backup, antivirus, etc.)
*Trace IDs:* none found (no backend errors correlated)

*Likely cause:* Recurring scheduled process on `prod-new-04` consuming ~50% CPU for ~15 min daily around 08:23 UTC. Centreon threshold fired on a transient blip that was already resolving. Not a production incident — no service disruption observed.

*Suggested next action:*
1. RDP to `prod-new-04` → check Windows Task Scheduler and SQL Server Agent jobs for tasks scheduled around 08:20–08:25 UTC
2. If this is a known/expected job (e.g. SQL maintenance, backup, log shipping), add to `kb/false-alarms.json` so future Centreon alerts from this check are auto-silenced
3. If the job is unknown or unexpected, investigate what process is running (Task Manager history, Event Viewer)

*Alert source:* Centreon Monitoring — 2026-05-04 06:19 EDT
:warning: _Alert attachment content is not accessible via Slack MCP (message body is empty — Centreon posts via rich attachments). Investigation is based entirely on corroborating Datadog signals._

*Symptoms:*
• APM metrics (request hits, error rate, latency) are completely absent for *all core services* (runtime-core-api, designer-core-api, ms-gateway-api) for the past *24 hours* — empty time series, no data at all
• Nginx connection metrics also absent
• Zero Datadog APM error logs in the past 2 hours
• Multiple monitors in `No Data` state: `runtime-core-api`, `designer-core-api`, `ms-account-api` and all their dependencies (Redis, SQL, MongoDB spans)
• Three *Warehouse Dashboard Network Test* synthetics failed at 09:31, 09:41, and 10:01 UTC today (just before this 10:19 UTC Centreon alert)
• *[Synthetics] Method UI Grid and Dropdown Performance Test Midnight run* still in Alert state (triggered midnight EDT)
• *Service Signup Availability SLO* has been in Alert since 2026-04-29
*What IS healthy:*
• RabbitMQ: both nodes (prod-rabbitmq-01, prod-rabbitmq-02) actively reporting to Datadog — memory ~700 MB / 500 MB (well under 3.15 GB threshold). ~2700 messages queued, slowly draining.
• A prior Centreon alert fired at 04:39 EDT today (~90 min before this one)
*Trace IDs:* none available (APM silent)

*Likely cause:* IIS app pool(s) down or Datadog APM tracer offline on the application servers. The silence pattern (APM flat for 24h, RabbitMQ infra-agent alive) is consistent with `microservices` IIS pool or `runtime-core` pool having stopped — per CLAUDE.md, either of those takes down the whole application tier. The Warehouse Network Test failures right before this alert may indicate the same or a related infrastructure host.

*Suggested next action:* Check IIS app pool status on the method-platform server — specifically `microservices.methodlocal.int`, `runtime-core`, and the Warehouse host. If pools are stopped, restart them and watch for recovery in Datadog APM within 2-3 minutes.

Alert time: 2026-05-04 11:29 UTC (Centreon Monitoring)

*Symptoms:*
• `prod-classic-01`: `system.mem.pct_usable` hit *2.5% free* at 12:21 UTC — memory is ACTIVELY DETERIORATING (was 8% free at 10:24 UTC, now 7% and trending down)
• `prod-classic-02`: hit 3% free at 10:42 UTC, then recovered to 11% at 11:28 UTC — likely auto-triggered IIS pool recycle
• `runtime-core-api` DD monitors: all in *No Data* state (APM traces not flowing, 0 request hits in last hour)
• Synthetics monitor `[Synthetics] Method UI Grid and Dropdown Performance Test Midnight run` (ID 123495390): currently *Alert* state
• Multiple customers experiencing *XHR `status_code: 0`* on `/gateway/syncutil/syncwidget/*/GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync` (gopowertrain2, indianaautomotiveequipment, crslaboratories, bindersincCo1, maconstructiongroup, wildcatstriping, sslintlcorp) — sync widget completely unavailable
• Frontend errors spiking: 100+ errors in last 5 min (ResizeObserver, Redux state errors, sync widget failures)
*Trace IDs:* None — APM is No Data for runtime-core-api (service may be down)

*Baseline comparison:* runtime-core-api APM has 0 hits in last hour vs normal traffic; memory at 2-7% free vs expected 20-30%

*Recent deploys:* None in last 8h. Last method-ui deploy: 2026-04-24 (10 days ago). No deploy correlation.

*Likely cause:* Memory pressure / slow leak on `prod-classic-01` IIS host. The IIS app pools (runtime-core, microservices, legacy) are accumulating memory — `prod-classic-02` self-healed (pool recycle), but `prod-classic-01` is still consuming and at critical levels. This is causing the syncutil backend to be unresponsive.

*Suggested next action:* Recycle IIS pools on `prod-classic-01` immediately (microservices + legacy + runtime-core pools). If memory climbs back rapidly after recycle, investigate which `w3wp.exe` process is leaking (SSH to classic-01, Task Manager / Process Explorer). Monitor `system.mem.pct_usable{host:prod-classic-01}` after recycle.

*Symptoms:*
• `/gateway/syncutil/syncwidget/<account>/GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync` returning HTTP 0 (no response) for *16+ customer accounts* — thejpcookecompany, EnglandLogistics, ir2017, deltakits1, elmusa, commair, boswellwindows3, firestationfurniture, amtax1040, JudicialServicesRR, wastecostsolutionsinc, and more
• `/apps/api/dashboardview/GetApps` also HTTP 0 for account `sitepreps` (confirms runtime-core Apps.Api path is broken too)
• All errors are status 0 (connection refused or port not responding) — not 5xx, not timeouts
• Synthetics "Method UI Grid and Dropdown Performance Test" failing on *both* us-east-1 and us-west-1 since 09:48–09:53 EDT, still Alert now (1h+ duration)
• XHR error Warn monitor (`Unusual number of XHR errors for account`) re-fired at 11:13 EDT — issue is *ongoing* at poll time
• Datadog APM for `runtime-core-api` has been *completely dark since 2026-05-03T00:13Z* (yesterday midnight) — zero request/error/latency series; all 6 runtime-core monitors stuck in "No Data"
• Bot B063S8NBW0M in #alert-runtime-monitoring fired 17 times in paired bursts: 10:02, 10:13, 10:21, 10:43, 10:55, 10:59, 11:04 EDT — consistent with a periodic health-check hitting dead endpoints every 10–15 min for 60+ min
*Timeline:*
• 09:48 EDT: Synthetics Day run fails (us-east-1)
• 09:53 EDT: Synthetics Day run 2 fails (us-west-1)
• 10:02 EDT: Runtime-monitoring alert storm begins (17 alerts)
• 10:03 EDT: Ismael manually recycled `methodwebservice` app pool (likely in response to the alerts)
• 10:06 EDT: Frontend-errors bot starts firing (23 alerts — XHR failures from real users)
• 10:54 EDT: Frontend-errors quiet down (incomplete recovery?)
• 11:05 EDT: Runtime-monitoring last alert
• 11:13 EDT: XHR Warn fires again → service still partially broken
*Trace IDs:* None available (Datadog APM dark for runtime-core-api since yesterday midnight; agent may have detached after a prior recycle/crash)

*Likely cause:* `methodwebservice` IIS app pool hosts both `syncutil` (ms-sync-util: the QBO sync widget) and the `runtime-core` Apps.Api path. The pool failed before 09:48 EDT; Ismael's 10:03 recycle did not fully restore it. The service appears to be either stopped, crash-looping, or listening on the wrong binding. Datadog APM dark since yesterday suggests the APM agent was lost in a prior overnight recycle and was never re-attached — this is a separate low-urgency issue but obscures today's diagnostics.

*Suggested next action:* Check IIS Manager on prod for `methodwebservice` pool state — if stopped or error state, start it; if running but unhealthy, check Windows Event Log / Application Log for startup exceptions. Also verify the Datadog agent service (`ddagent`) is running and restart it if not, to restore APM visibility.

> :warning: Groups 2 (#alert-frontend-errors, 23 alerts) and 3 (#alert-system Centreon, 1 alert) are also firing in this same window — see separate DMs. All three likely share this root cause.
